note: Pre-registered before the R3-R15 replay (2026-10-06), from the rejection messages recorded in the mainline stores and the side runs. Rules are tried in order against the first issue of a recorded rejected attempt; the first match decides. 'expect' is what the new code should do with that answer: accept (the rejection was a copied identity code now binds), reject (a source or semantic gate that must hold), reject_known_gap (should be code-bound but is not yet). Attempts that are not rejections are counted separately: transport failures, check verdicts, budget closure.

rules.label: CI parent_basis copied wrong
rules.pattern: CI names a different parent basis

rules.label: assessment evidence_refs locators invented
rules.pattern: candidate sources must cite a resolvable user text span or event;.*evidence_refs

rules.label: Atom authority.basis selector out of range
rules.pattern: candidate sources must cite a resolvable user text span or event;.*authority\.(basis|rules)

rules.label: expected_revision copied wrong
rules.pattern: expected_revision \d+ does not match current \d+(?!: ir_changes\[\d+\] \([^)]*\) (earlier in this group|in an earlier group of this batch) already changed)

rules.label: assessment basis.event_ids copied wrong
rules.pattern: must name this batch's events in basis\.event_ids

rules.label: coverage.refs names an Atom version that is not the plan's current one
rules.pattern: points to an Atom revision .* that is not the current one

rules.label: segment_id plus a quote inside that segment (then a selector conflict)
rules.amended: added after the first full replay (2026-10-06): R10 mgmt-20 #0 gives segment s8 and a quote equal to that segment's text; c65a94f selects a quote inside the segment it names. Decided from the recorded answer, not from the new outcome: every reference that gives both a segment_id and a quote has the quote inside that segment of the request, and selector_conflict is the only defect the message names. Otherwise the rejection stays B.

rules.label: adopted text classified as non-normative or superseded
normative source dropped without a superseded disposition
rules.pattern: was dropped without an explicit superseded disposition

rules.label: IR source selector does not resolve (quote, segment, span, wrong event, placeholder)
IR group task or identity duplicated
rules.pattern: Each IR group must have one distinct task

rules.label: same IR object changed twice in one batch

separate.transport: a recorded attempt with a failure diagnostic and no answer text: not a rejection, not counted as flip or regression
separate.check: an independent check verdict; fed back as recorded and marked not comparable, inconsistent verdicts counted on their own
separate.budget: a batch closed for budget (B4); counted on its own
separate.unclassified: a recorded rejection no rule matches; listed for review
